clue.text: Result from heated serial inflation, say?

definitions.text: Result from heated serial inflation, say?

parts.words: Result from heated serial inflation, say?
parts.note: serial is read as its sound-twin cereal: maize kernels heated until they swell and burst produce a cinema snack

explanation.surface: Someone asks what comes of a heated, inflationary series of events.
explanation.definitionFit: Heating dried maize kernels makes them swell and burst open into the fluffy snack, so it is literally what heated cereal inflates into.

clue.text: Nelson on track to lose foot, taking umbrage!

indicators.note: the foot of a word is its last letter, which is to be dropped here

parts.note: Nelson Piquet was a Brazilian Formula One world champion, a racing driver on the track

explanation.surface: A racing driver loses a foot in a crash and is understandably resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose foot' drops the final T of PIQUET; 'taking' simply links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name resentment at a slight, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Playwright with small part, usual failure …

indicators.note: a failure is a breakdown, so the letters collapse and are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: pt is the standard abbreviation of part, a small form of the word

explanation.surface: A dramatist given only a bit part reports the usual flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failure' tells you to rearrange PT plus USUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Maccius Plautus was a Roman comic dramatist, so he is an example of a playwright.

clue.text: … speaking of the same poet

indicators.note: speaking signals that the phrase is pronounced, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: following on from the previous clue, 'of the same' means of it, referring back to that thing

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a remark about the same poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 2 down: 'the same' stands for 'it', and 'of it' said quickly sounds like the Roman poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Publius Ovidius Naso, author of the Metamorphoses, was a Roman poet.

clue.text: Doctrine of 21's son: leaderless Americans vote madly

indicators.note: madly means wildly, signalling that the combined letters are thrown into a new order
a leaderless word loses its first letter, its head

explanation.surface: A president's son is defeated as headless Americans vote wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across is BUSH, so the definition is Bush's doctrine. 'leaderless' removes the A from AMERICANS, giving MERICANS; 'madly' rearranges SON + MERICANS + VOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawkish right-wing political creed associated with George W Bush's administration was widely labelled by this name.

clue.text: One-man band's performance over chaps who are paid for their performance

definitions.text: chaps who are paid for their performance

parts.note: a gig is a performance by a musician or band

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a one-man effort is a solo

explanation.surface: A busker's set goes on longer than planned for men who expect to be paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-man band' reads as one phrase, but it splits: a one-man show is a solo, and 'over' turns it round to OLOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Men paid by women for companionship and sex are called this, so the phrase describes them.

clue.text: Why no Republican gain in the Napa Valley? It speaks for itself!

definitions.text: Why no Republican gain in the Napa Valley? It speaks for itself!

parts.words: Why no Republican gain in the Napa Valley? It speaks for itself!
parts.note: Napa Valley grows fine wine and votes Democrat; the president's surname doubles as the old vintner's sign, an ivy ... hung outside a tavern, which quality drink does without

explanation.surface: A political commentator explains why California's wine country rejects the Republican president.
explanation.walkthrough: A bush was once hung outside a tavern to advertise wine; the proverb says good wine needs no advertising. Here the bush is also President Bush, a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: The old proverb means that something of real quality needs no advertising, so it speaks for itself.

clue.text: Duplicity involving many in parliamentary restriction

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: guile is crafty deceit, which is duplicity
a lot means many

explanation.surface: Deceit and a large number of people combine in Parliament's limits on debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parliamentary restriction' is the Commons procedure that timetables debate, named after the French execution device; 'involving' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament this is the procedure that sets a fixed timetable cutting off debate on a bill, a restriction on discussion.

clue.text: W.C. Fields providing one for visitors?

definitions.text: W.C. Fields providing one for visitors?

parts.words: W.C. Fields providing one for visitors?
parts.note: read not as the comedian but as a water closet out in the fields, a temporary toilet laid on for those camping there

explanation.surface: The American comedian W.C. Fields lays something on for his guests.
explanation.walkthrough: W.C. Fields, the comedian, misleads: read W.C. as toilet and Fields as open ground, where a camp provides a crude privy.
explanation.definitionFit: A crude communal toilet dug in a camp or the open ground is exactly a field water closet.

clue.text: Makeshift plughole?

definitions.meaning: a temporary substitute used until something better is found
playfully, a gap that a stop fills, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: A temporary measure filling a gap is a makeshift, and taken literally the term names something that plugs a hole.

clue.text: Parisian ringer's ring from a phone card in jail

indicators.note: ring from means the ring piece follows what it comes out of
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: quod is old British slang for prison
a SIM is the card inside a mobile phone
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A Paris bell-ringer calls someone from a phone in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A + SIM inside QUOD; 'from' sets the O (ring) after that. The 's of ringer's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugo's hunchback of Notre-Dame rings the cathedral bells in Paris, so he is the Parisian bell-ringer.

clue.text: Cleft splint won't support it

indicators.note: the words hold up and carry the answer within them, as a support holds something

explanation.surface: A broken bone will not be held by a splint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support it' says the run of letters inside 'splint won't' carries the answer: splINT WOn't.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleft is the past participle of cleave, meaning split down the middle.

clue.text: Waste disposal with disposed of worries

indicators.note: disposal means arrangement, signalling the letters are set out afresh
disposed of means got rid of, so the named letter is removed

explanation.surface: A kitchen waste-disposal unit and its removal cause anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed of' removes W (with) from WASTE to leave ASTE; 'disposal' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that worries you is said to be gnawing at or consuming you, as in 'what's bothering him?'

clue.text: 505 making it, if humanly possible

definitions.meaning: in Roman numerals 505 is DV, the abbreviation of Latin deo volente
a phrase used to mean provided circumstances allow

explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 and V is 5, so 505 is DV, short for the Latin deo volente; 'making it' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Deo volente translates as the English phrase, a hope that things go to plan if nothing prevents them.

clue.text: 21 senior's utterance falling on deaf ears?

definitions.meaning: 21 is the elder president, whose 1988 campaign pledge on taxes became this catchphrase
playfully, words spoken so that the hard of hearing can follow from the mouth

explanation.walkthrough: 21 across is BUSH; the senior is George H W Bush, who promised 'no new taxes' with this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what George H W Bush said, and literally it asks a deaf listener to lip-read.

clue.text: Size up Jenny?

definitions.meaning: to size up is to evaluate
a jenny is a female donkey, and -ess makes a feminine form, so jokily a she-ass

explanation.definitionFit: To size up is to evaluate, and jokily a she-ass would be an ass with the feminine ending -ess.

clue.text: Shallow river in no part ebbing

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the river inside the other letters
ebbing means flowing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A river that has receded everywhere is now very low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ebbing' (the tide flowing back) reverses only the abbreviation for part, giving TP; 'in' signals that the river goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow water is literally water lacking depth, so the phrase is an exact paraphrase.

clue.text: Court champion by putting the shot inside

indicators.note: putting signals placing one piece somewhere
inside says where the piece goes, within the other

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
lead is the metal of shot fired from a gun

explanation.surface: An athlete champion at the shot put is introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about putting the shot in athletics; 'putting ... inside' is split around the thing put, which is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues a case in a law court is a pleader, a champion of a client's cause.

clue.text: Decisive celebrity toppling old chess champ

indicators.note: toppling in a down clue means turning over, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person, a celebrity
Mikhail Tal was world chess champion in 1960

explanation.surface: A famous figure topples a former chess champion in a decisive game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toppling' turns VIP into PIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pivotal is the point on which everything turns, so it is crucial or decisive.

clue.text: Old forty-niner's title call

parts.note: ex means former or old
a forty-niner was a California gold prospector of 1849, whose title to a plot was a claim

explanation.surface: An old gold prospector's title deed is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The forty-niners were the 1849 California Gold Rush miners, who staked a claim to land.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out suddenly is to call out, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: A score more than one's allotment

definitions.text: A score more than one's allotment

parts.words: A score more than one's allotment
parts.note: the biblical allotted human lifespan is threescore years and ten, seventy; add another twenty

explanation.surface: Someone takes twenty more than their share.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible gives the span of life as threescore years and ten (70); a score (20) more is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventy, the traditional allotted lifespan, plus a score of twenty gives this number of years.

clue.text: Corrosive influence in support of the Guardian

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball
rust corrodes iron

explanation.surface: Something corrosive is supporting this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the' links; the capital G tempts you to read the newspaper, but it is just a guardian, someone holding property in trust; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A person holding property in trust for others acts as its legal guardian, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: An element of collaboration?

parts.note: the wartime French regime that collaborated with Germany was based at a spa town, and water is one of the four classical elements

explanation.surface: Someone asks what part cooperation plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Vichy, the French spa town, gave its name to the collaborationist government of 1940-44; water is one of the four classical elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Mineral water bottled from the springs at the spa town is literally an element from the collaborators' capital.

clue.text: See 5 down
His surprise was noted

parts.note: the Surprise is a famous symphony, and noted means set down in musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone's astonishment was observed.
explanation.walkthrough: Symphony No 94 is nicknamed the Surprise for its sudden loud chord; 'noted' means written in notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian composer wrote the Surprise Symphony, so his surprise was literally put into notes.

clue.text: Lincoln died in his sleep

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln
d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: President Lincoln passed away peacefully overnight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Lincoln died in his sleep, but he was assassinated.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in bed, as a sleeper is, is the meaning of the adverb.

clue.text: Time Omar broadcast with earflaps

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Time Omar broadcast with earflaps (5)' for TRAGI: T (time) leaves RAGI, which no reading of 'Omar broadcast' gives, and a search of the exact text found nothing

clue.text: Tiny thing Mrs Fawlty left off Torquay's statistical year initially

parts.note: it can mean a thing, as in 'what is it?'

indicators.note: left off means L (left) is dropped

parts.note: Sybil Fawlty is the hotelier's wife in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, set in Torquay

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Fawlty Towers' Sybil leaves out the Torquay hotel's annual statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left off' removes L from SYBIL; 'initially' takes T, S, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The reduplicated nursery word means very small, a synonym of tiny.

clue.text: Single payment for tax evaders?

definitions.meaning: one payment of the whole amount at once
the lump was the British system of casual building workers paid in cash, dodging income tax

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the lump' was casual building labour paid cash in hand to evade tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole amount paid in one go is a single payment, and the lump suggests a sum for cash-in-hand workers.

clue.text: Youthful pulse couldn't shoulder it, mate!

definitions.meaning: a pulse is a legume; a young one could not carry the label of an aged legume
an old-fashioned British term of address for a friend

explanation.walkthrough: A pulse is a bean; a young bean could not bear the name of an aged one. The second sense is dated British slang for a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dated upper-class British way of addressing a friend, equivalent to mate.
